entries.text: B1 Who carries out the restart of the web server The new `/restart-web` command must stop the control room, rebuild its page, and start it again. Today the engine and dispatcher have no handle on the web process: the supervisor owns it. Until we decide who does the work, the spec cannot say which side builds what. a) The supervisor does it. The command goes to the engine as usual, the engine asks the supervisor (through its registration or PID files), and the supervisor stops the web child, run…
entries.answer: a) The supervisor does it. The command goes to the engine as usual, the engine asks the supervisor (through its registration or PID files), and the supervisor stops the web child, runs the build, and starts it again. Answered by hermes on 2026-11-13

entries.text: B2 What `/restart-web` does when there is no supervisor `openlanes web` can also run alone, for example after a run has ended, with no supervisor and no engine. In that case no process is watching the web server, and a command that kills it would leave nothing to start it again. a) Refuse with a clear reply: "`/restart-web` needs `openlanes start`; no supervisor is running." (Recommended) b) Restart anyway, by having the web server re-execute itself after the build. c) Do not offer the command …
entries.answer: a) Refuse with a clear reply: "`/restart-web` needs `openlanes start`; no supervisor is running." Answered by hermes on 2026-11-13

entries.text: B3 How the page gets rebuilt, and where The page is built with `npm run build` in `web/`, which needs Node and the page's sources. An installed gem ships the built `web/dist` and may not have either. A restart that cannot build would serve the old page. a) Run `npm run build` in the gem's `web/` directory. If Node or the sources are missing, or the build fails, keep the old page, restart the server anyway, and report the failure in the reply. (Recommended) b) The same, but when the build fails,…
entries.answer: a) Run `npm run build` in the gem's `web/` directory. If Node or the sources are missing, or the build fails, keep the old page, restart the server anyway, and report the failure in the reply. Answered by hermes on 2026-11-13

entries.text: B4 What the copilot should do now that it is no longer read-only The brief asks that the copilot agent move from haiku/low to Sonnet, report on the status of each command sent to a worker, and report general stats like the log printed when OpenLanes stops. This changes `agents/copilot.md`, its read-only boundary in `operator.rb`, and the cost of every chat message. Which is meant? a) Change only the model to Sonnet and the README wording. The copilot still acts only through the slash grammar an…
entries.answer: a) Change only the model to Sonnet and the README wording. The copilot still acts only through the slash grammar and buttons, and gains read-only commands that print status and run statistics. Answered by hermes on 2026-11-13
